key_findings: OpenSourceMalware named the campaign React2STEAL and identified 45 repositories across 44 GitHub accounts running a scan.yml GitHub Actions workflow.

The pipeline tries React2Shell (CVE-2025-55182), the CVE-2025-29927 middleware bypass and an SSRF through /_next/image to cloud instance metadata, then collects environment variables, credentials and config files.
At least 1,281 unique victim hostnames across about 1,100 domains were found; results were still being committed about every 11 minutes on November 17.
OpenSourceMalware lists the threat actor as unknown and says it does not know whether the same operator ran the earlier wfx-loot campaign.
recommendations: Upgrade React and Next.js to fixed versions.
Strip or reject x-middleware-subrequest at the proxy or WAF until upgraded.
Rotate every secret the server could reach and enforce IMDSv2.

events.summary: OpenSourceMalware published research on November 18 on a campaign it named React2STEAL: 45 GitHub repositories across 44 accounts run scanners for React2Shell (CVE-2025-55182) and CVE-2025-29927 and commit results to public repositories. events.action: Verify WinRAR and other tools on your network are the publisher's signed copies; apply application allowlisting and code-signing checks, and alert on memory that is read, write and execute at once and on PNGs with truncated headers.
events.exec: Trusted programs can be rewritten into malware carriers whose fingerprint changes every run, so hash-based blocking is weak.
events.plain: Security firm ReversingLabs describes BubbleLoader, malware that edits ordinary programs like WinRAR so they secretly load other malware, and changes its fingerprint every time it runs.

key_findings: BubbleLoader patches the entry point of a benign program and appends two PNG files; the host then decrypts and reflectively loads a final payload in memory.
Hosts seen include WinRAR, x64dbg, Windows Media Player, a Firefox launcher and virtiofs; the post names no victims or sectors and the final payload varies by sample.
Earliest samples date from February 2026, with two activity clusters in mid-September and early October.

It overwrites padding bytes in the payload with timestamp-derived randomness on each run, so the in-memory hash changes every execution, and hooks RtlPcToFileHeader in ntdll so the payload can handle exceptions.
The second PNG is a fake with a truncated header, which ReversingLabs offers as a static detection signal; the post does not say how the altered programs reach victims.
recommendations: Enforce strict application allowlisting and code-signing verification, especially for common utilities such as WinRAR.
Have EDR alert on read-write-execute memory allocated with VirtualAlloc and on protection changes to the ntdll routine RtlPcToFileHeader.
Add static rules for embedded PNGs with a truncated header.
Rely on behavioural memory analysis and entry-point integrity checks, not only static payload hashes.

events.summary: ReversingLabs analysed BubbleLoader, a loader that rewrites a few instructions at a program's entry point and adds two PNG images to turn legitimate software, including WinRAR and Windows Media Player, into a carrier for other malware. It changes its payload's in-memory hash on every run. Samples date from February 2026, with activity clusters in September and October. Delivery method is not stated.
events.title: ReversingLabs: BubbleLoader turns WinRAR and other programs into malware carriers

validation.note: ReversingLabs original (highlights and intro read; full body only summarised) and Help Net Security's detailed write-up, which restates the vendor research.

review.note: Facts match ReversingLabs and Help Net Security; removed supply-chain tag as source states no supply-chain compromise

events.action: Upgrade Ruby to 4.0.10, 3.4.13 or 3.3.14. Do not compile or match regular expressions from untrusted input, and plan to move off Ruby 3.2 and earlier, which get no fix.

Several could allow remote code execution in some scenarios, notably where attacker-controlled patterns are compiled.
Maintainers say they are aware of proof-of-concept code that shows remote code execution for some; GBHackers says the disclosure reported no active exploitation.
Ruby 3.2 and earlier are end of life and will not be fixed.
recommendations: Upgrade to a fixed release.
Avoid compiling attacker-controlled regular expressions.

events.title: TU Berlin researchers bypass firmware-TPM lockout to crack Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs (CVE-2026-43613)
events.summary: TU Berlin researchers reset the lockout counter of firmware TPMs by replacing the flash chip, letting an attacker with physical access guess Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs far faster. A 6-digit BitLocker PIN fell in 236 tries. AMD tracks it as CVE-2026-43613 (CVSS 5.1) with fixes planned November 2026 to February 2027; Intel reports no flaw in its component. Lab only.
events.plain: Researchers showed that someone holding a laptop can reset its PIN-guess limit by swapping a chip, then crack the PIN in days instead of years.
events.exec: Requires physical access and hardware modification, so the risk is for lost or stolen laptops; no exploitation reported.
events.action: Use long alphanumeric PINs or TPM plus startup key for BitLocker on high-risk laptops, and apply AMD firmware updates as they ship.

key_findings: Flash-chip replacement resets the 32-try lockout on firmware TPMs.
4-digit Hello PIN worst case 40 hours versus 69 days; 6-digit BitLocker PIN 20 days versus 19 years.
AMD fixes planned Nov 2026 to Feb 2027; Intel and Microsoft issued no CVE.
recommendations: Stronger PINs; apply AMD firmware updates.

validation.note: Read via fetch agent; cites arXiv 2611.18126, AMD SB-7079 and Intel notice, not opened.

review.note: THN Nov 18: CVE-2026-43613 CVSS 5.1, 236 tries, AMD fix Nov-Feb 2027, Intel no flaw, lab only match.

key_findings: Targets were 7 semiconductor and advanced-manufacturing firms, 3 defence or defence-policy bodies and 4 human-rights or civil-society groups, including a Canadian rights body and a US teachers' union.
The cluster ran 25 operations against at least 19 organisations and reached confirmed unauthorised access or data retrieval at 10 of them.
It used a customised fork of the open-source Cairn framework driven by Zhipu GLM 5.2 and DeepSeek V4 models, plus a custom skill pack not in upstream Cairn.
Entry came from password spraying, brute-forced credentials, unauthenticated cloud-storage writes, login bypasses and open registration endpoints rather than new exploits.
Data taken included over 1 million union member records, about 31,000 CRM contacts and about 150,000 internal documents; Unit 42 assesses China-nexus collection with moderate confidence.
recommendations: Tighten identity hygiene: remove weak, default and shared passwords on internet-facing applications.
Reduce the exposed attack surface, including open registration endpoints and unauthenticated cloud storage.
Patch software affected by older public CVEs.
Monitor for the two IP addresses Unit 42 published for the Cairn hosting and staging servers.

events.action: Log and inspect QUIC traffic or block outbound UDP 443 so it falls back to inspectable TCP. Patch Exchange and web servers, review accounts holding the ApplicationImpersonation role and audit Group Policy logon scripts for changes.
events.actor: TGR-STA-0049 (also REF7707, Earth Alux, Ink Dragon)
events.exec: Espionage tools now hide in HTTP/3 traffic that many network monitors skip; unpatched Exchange servers remain the way in.
events.plain: Researchers found a spying group breaking into government networks in Southeast Asia through unpatched email servers and hiding its remote-control traffic inside a newer web protocol many security tools do not inspect.

key_findings: Targets are Southeast Asian government entities; one decoy PDF imitates a Myanmar election commission document, though victim countries are not confirmed.
Entry is through unpatched Microsoft Exchange and web servers to plant web shells, with phishing using decoy PDFs and DLL sideloading as a second route.
PerfectPioneer, a Go tool with six variants, uses HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 depending on the variant (one variant uses HTTP/3 with HTTP/2 fallback); two variants add a blocklist of dangerous commands.
KUKURAT loads at least 12 modules for keylogging, screenshots, lateral movement and tunnelling, and creates decoy network, registry and file activity.
Activity spans about nine months and included mass mailbox permission changes on Exchange and credential theft from a domain controller.
recommendations: Log and inspect QUIC traffic, or block outbound UDP 443 so HTTP/3 falls back to inspectable TCP.
Audit SYSVOL and Group Policy for unauthorised logon script changes.
Create behavioural rules for rundll32.exe loading comsvcs.dll, including ordinal-based calls.
Review accounts with the ApplicationImpersonation role and watch Exchange logs for repeated Add-MailboxPermission FullAccess grants.

events.summary: Unit 42 describes about nine months of intrusions into Southeast Asian government networks by a group it tracks as TGR-STA-0049. The attackers entered through unpatched Microsoft Exchange and web servers, then deployed two custom remote access tools, PerfectPioneer and KUKURAT, that talk to their controllers over HTTP/3. KUKURAT also generates decoy activity to hide what it is doing.

events.exec: An unpatched Linux kernel flaw lets an attacker who already runs code on a server, including inside a container, become root on the host.

Chained with one of its five nginx flaws, it gave root on the host, including from a Docker container; Xint withholds most exploit details until a kernel patch exists.
No CVE number or kernel patch is stated; Xint says the patch will come in the coming weeks (nginx2root.com).
A post on oss-security (Rich Felker, 18 November) advises anyone not needing SCTP to block the module.
recommendations: Block the sctp module where not needed.
Apply kernel updates when released.

events.title: Yuma Regional Medical Center to pay $1,985,000 to settle 2022 ransomware data breach lawsuit
events.date_note: HIPAA Journal's publication day; the settlement is reported on that day. The attack itself was April 21-25, 2022.
events.summary: HIPAA Journal reports a $1,985,000 settlement fund in the class action Dillon Clarke, et al. v. Yuma Regional Medical Center (D. Arizona) over a ransomware attack in which hackers accessed systems between April 21 and April 25, 2022. 738,145 individuals were reported to HHS OCR; names, Social Security numbers, health insurance and limited medical information were involved. The center denies the claims and wrongdoing.
events.plain: A hospital in Arizona agreed to a $1,985,000 settlement of a lawsuit over a 2022 ransomware attack that exposed data of 738,145 people, according to a news report.
events.exec: Data breach litigation can cost millions years after an attack, even when the organisation denies liability.
events.action: No action needed; for awareness. Affected patients should check the settlement notice for claim deadlines.
events.impact: 738,145 individuals reported to HHS OCR; individual reimbursement capped at $4,000 for documented losses, plus one year of medical data monitoring.

sources.name: HIPAA Journal: Yuma Regional Medical Center data breach settlement

validation.note: Only HIPAA Journal read; court filings not read. Its settlement deadlines look inconsistent and are omitted.

review.note: Fund amount, case, attack dates, 738,145 OCR figure, data types, 4,000 cap, denial checked against HIPAA Journal 20 Nov; single_source correct

events.title: Rapid7 adds Metasploit modules for two Zimbra flaws, an email-impersonation bypass and a GraphQL login rate-limit bypass
events.summary: Rapid7's Metasploit wrap-up of 20 November adds two Zimbra auxiliary modules, so public exploit code now exists for both. One, for CVE-2026-73571 (SaveDraftRequest), lets an ordinary authenticated user send mail as another local mailbox; Rapid7 tested it on Zimbra 10.1.16. The other, for CVE-2026-93637, bypasses the GraphQL authentication rate limit and was validated on 10.1.16 Network Edition. The post gives no fixed versions.
events.plain: Rapid7 published ready-made Metasploit test modules for two Zimbra mail-server flaws, one letting a logged-in user send mail as someone else.
events.exec: Public Metasploit modules now exist for two Zimbra flaws, which makes testing and misuse easier.
events.action: Check Zimbra's own advisories for CVE-2026-73571 and CVE-2026-93637 and apply any fix; the Rapid7 post names no fixed version.

key_findings: CVE-2026-73571: authenticated user can send mail as another local mailbox.
CVE-2026-93637: GraphQL authentication rate-limit bypass.
CVE-2026-73571 module tested on Zimbra 10.1.16; CVE-2026-93637 module validated on 10.1.16 Network Edition.
recommendations: Check Zimbra's advisories for fixes.

validation.note: Read the Rapid7 post only; Zimbra's advisory was not read.

review.note: Rapid7 post: both modules and CVEs match; Network Edition is stated only for CVE-2026-93637, so summary and key finding now say so (73571 tested on 10.1.16). Single-source kept; no fixed versions in post.

events.title: ZOZO: about 15.18 million ZOZOTOWN customers' data leaked via PLAID KARTE breach
events.summary: ZOZO said on 20 November that customer information it managed on PLAID's KARTE leaked. About 15.18 million ZOZOTOWN customers incl. former members (member ID, age, gender, postal code) are affected, about 47,000 of them also with login name, email and phone number; about 13.93 million WEAR by ZOZO customers; about 24,000 brand staff. Passwords are not managed in KARTE; card data is not confirmed leaked.

events.action: Ask Zyxel support or your ISP for the firmware listed in Zyxel's advisory and install it; for ISP-supplied devices, contact the ISP because the device may have custom settings.
events.exec: Zyxel says WAN access is disabled by default on these devices; the advisory does not say either flaw is exploited.
events.plain: Zyxel has released fixes for two flaws in many of its DSL and fiber modems and Wi-Fi extenders. One could let an attacker with no login run commands on the device through a crafted web request.

key_findings: CVE-2026-79614 is an out-of-bounds write in libclinkc.so that could let an unauthenticated attacker elevate privileges and potentially execute arbitrary commands through a crafted HTTP request.
CVE-2026-86676 is a post-authentication command injection; it can succeed only if user-configured passwords have been compromised.
The advisory lists 48 models for the first CVE and 30 for the second and says WAN access is disabled by default.
recommendations: Install the patched firmware; ISP-supplied devices: contact the ISP.

events.summary: Zyxel's advisory of November 17 covers CVE-2026-79614, an out-of-bounds write that could let an unauthenticated attacker elevate privileges and potentially execute arbitrary commands via a crafted HTTP request, and CVE-2026-86676, a post-authentication command injection. It lists 48 and 30 affected DSL/Ethernet CPE, fiber ONT and wireless extender models and says WAN access is disabled by default. It makes no statement on exploitation.
events.title: Zyxel patches out-of-bounds write and command injection flaws in DSL and fiber modems and Wi-Fi extenders

validation.note: Zyxel's own advisory read in full; Security.nl reports it.

review.note: Re-read Zyxel advisory and Security.nl: 17 Nov, both CVE descriptions, 48 and 30 models, WAN off by default, no exploitation statement

analysis/latest.summary: Patch first what is already being exploited: Google says a PRC-nexus actor used the vCenter authentication bypass CVE-2026-123890 as a zero-day, F6 reports Cisco Expressway clusters breached after public exploit code (Cisco has not confirmed), and Confluence, N-central, ScreenConnect technician clients, Apache Roller and four flaws CISA listed on Nov 18 are under attack; Beazley says exploited flaws now start 28% of its ransomware cases. NGINX2Root remains the broadest exposure. Supplier breaches keep reaching customers: PLAID KARTE, Fireworks AI, and now Amadeus (Thai Airways) and a DAOU Office update that installed malicious files. South Korea disclosed a government email hack and a run of university breaches. US officials told Congress the November outage wave was not a cyberattack; the outages remain a cluster in time only.

patterns.title: NGINX2Root: HTTP/2 code execution, public exploit code, and appliances that bundle NGINX
patterns.narrative: F5 shipped fixes for five NGINX flaws. Two in HTTP/2 handling, CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633, let an unauthenticated attacker run code as the nginx worker; Wiz says CVE-2026-123007 affects every version since 1.9.5, and fixes are in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9. CERT-FR knows of a public proof of concept and SecurityWeek says Rapid7 and Censys published one. Xint, which found the flaws, chained one with a separate, still-unpatched Linux kernel SCTP bug to reach root, including out of a Docker container. NGINX fronts a large share of web services and sits inside ingress controllers and appliances, so this is the week's broadest exposure. On Nov 19 Synology listed the same CVE-2026-123007 among fixes for its DSM storage operating system, the first appliance vendor on file to do so, and CERT-SE issued its own warning. Disabling HTTP/2 is CERT-FR's interim workaround.
patterns.caveat: No exploitation in the wild is reported by F5, CERT-FR, Wiz or SecurityWeek. Sources differ on whose proof of concept is public (Wiz withholds its own), and F5's own advisory could not be read. The kernel flaw has no CVE and Xint withholds its details. The Apache mod_http2 flaw that Singapore says is exploited is in different software and is grouped here only because the protocol is the same. Synology's advisory does not say whether its NGINX build is reachable over HTTP/2 by default.

edges.rel: chained to kernel bug for root (Xint)

patterns.title: Exploited now: vCenter, Expressway, Confluence, N-central, ScreenConnect and other edge systems
patterns.narrative: Exploitation is reported for a run of internet-facing and management systems this week. Google says the PRC-nexus actor ARMORY CASTLE exploited the VMware vCenter authentication bypass CVE-2026-123890 as a zero-day, with Rapid7 dating activity to September. The firm F6 investigated an intrusion through Cisco Expressway clusters after proof-of-concept code was posted for CVE-2026-76466. CISA listed the Apache Axis flaw behind Confluence takeovers, plus Synology DSM, LiteLLM and REDCap flaws, as exploited; N-central servers were hit through zero-days; Apache says the Roller flaw is exploited; Singapore warns of Apache mod_http2 exploitation; CISA added Puppet Enterprise and Check Point Gaia; Huntress tracks rogue ScreenConnect clients pushed to hundreds of hosts and, separately, exploitation of ScreenConnect flaw CVE-2026-84869 against MSP technicians' own workstations, which a server update alone does not fix; and Dorsata was breached through a Metabase zero-day. Old flaws still pay off: OpenSourceMalware's React2STEAL scanners exploit React2Shell and a Next.js flaw patched months ago and publish stolen secrets on GitHub. Beazley Security says exploited vulnerabilities started 28% of its ransomware cases in Q3, double Q2, and Dragos says industrial ransomware this quarter mostly entered through edge devices, which matches this list. These are the patches to apply before the merely critical ones.
patterns.caveat: Each exploitation claim is about one product and is stated by an agency, vendor or investigating firm, but they are different attackers; grouping them is by attribute. Cisco's advisory still says Cisco knows of no malicious use of the Expressway flaw, so that case rests on F6 as reported by SecurityWeek. Rapid7 says the Confluence and N-central exploitation was reported together, not that one actor did both. The Dorsata intrusion happened in August. The two ScreenConnect reports concern different flaws and Huntress does not tie them to one actor. Beazley's figures come from its own caseload, reported second-hand by Insurance Business.

patterns.title: Critical fixes with public exploit code but no attacks reported yet
patterns.narrative: A second tier of flaws has fixes and, in several cases, public exploit code, but no reported attacks. CISA told organisations to patch the Java4Shell flaw CVE-2026-114938 immediately, and Oracle's November update carries the fix. Depthfirst published phpAfterShell, which reaches code execution on PHP's default session handler despite October's PHP2Shell fixes, the same day PHP shipped releases fixing 17 flaws. Depthfirst also published database exploits for PostgreSQL, MySQL, ClickHouse and Oracle. NCSC Netherlands knows of public exploit code for Ivanti Endpoint Manager; Drupal, WordPress, F5 BIG-IP and Synology DSM shipped critical fixes; SonicWall says Gen 6 firewalls will get no more patches. Australia's ACSC warns that the gap between disclosure and exploitation keeps shrinking, which is why public code matters more than a score.
patterns.caveat: No exploitation is reported for any of these at the time of writing; that public code will soon be used is our inference, drawn from the pattern in the exploited list, not a finding. The research exploits have not been independently reproduced, and the sources do not say which PHP release fixes phpAfterShell.

edges.rel: same day, likely same PHP releases

patterns.title: Breached suppliers with named customers: PLAID KARTE and Fireworks AI
patterns.narrative: Two supplier breaches now have customers that say they were hit through them. PLAID suspended its KARTE customer-data service after unauthorized access on Nov 13, with account emails and integration credentials listed as leaked. On Nov 18 BASE FOOD said about 710,000 customer names and emails linked to KARTE leaked, and DHC said about 19.11 million online-shop customer records leaked after the KARTE access. Fireworks AI confirmed two intrusions on Nov 17, the second exposing account and billing data for every account made before Oct 30; Cursor says a key it issued to Fireworks led to trojanized Claude Code extension builds, Notion says some AI chat transcripts were accessed, and Uber's breach of about 150,000 people is reported as involving Fireworks. Each supplier held data or keys for many customers, so more notices are likely.
patterns.caveat: PLAID's own notice was read only through a secondary summary, and DHC's figures come from NHK, Kyodo and Yomiuri. Sources do not always say which Fireworks incident reached which customer, and the Uber link rests on a spokesperson statement reported second-hand. Other KARTE or Fireworks customers have not been named, so counts will change.

patterns.title: Breaches through a provider, not the front door
patterns.narrative: Beyond the two named cascades, many confirmed breaches this week came through a supplier. Swiss federal pension fund Publica must assume member data leaked from a test environment after an attack on its software supplier PK Softech; about 40 Irish credit unions were exposed through Wellington IT; DHL employee data was copied from a survey provider; Office Partner's customer data was reached at an external service provider. JPMorganChase says vendors that serve it were attacked and marketing data with some customer names and emails was accessed, while Mastercard and Visa reported provider incidents the same day. Boone County, Indiana, says its employees' health data was exposed through Marathon Health, which runs its clinic. Optimizely's injected script reached 178 organisations' sites, and N-able disclosed access to a Mail Assure and SpamExperts server. Infoblox, La Poste's Maileva and Osaka's email delivery service add to the list. Two more on file: Thai Airways says its reservation provider Amadeus told it an unauthorised person reached about 60,500 booking records held in Amadeus's system, and South Korea's DAOU Office says its Windows messenger's automatic update installed malicious files on some users' PCs overnight on 15 to 16 November.
patterns.caveat: These are separate vendors and separate attackers; the shared element is the route, not the actor, and grouping them is our inference. JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard have not named their providers or said whether it is the same one; the n0n gang's claim is unverified. N-able says it has no evidence customer mail was compromised. Amadeus serves many airlines, but only Thai Airways has disclosed on file; whether others are affected is unknown. DAOU Office's notice is reported by DailySecu and gives no count of infected PCs.

edges.rel: same day, providers not named, link unknown

patterns.title: AI-driven attack tooling (ARTEX, Cairn)
patterns.narrative: The FBI, Cisco Talos, Amazon and Cloudflare each describe intrusions or scanning run with the open-source ARTEX agent platform; Cloudflare says AI pentest traffic rose about 30-fold since October. Google reports a PRC-nexus group building its own automated attack tool and an exploit_agent framework that turned patches into working exploits. The European Commission's spokesman confirmed on Nov 19 that the attack first detected on Oct 22, which took down its Sysper HR system and the JSIS health insurance scheme, was carried out with a publicly available AI tool; the Commission found no staff-wide data breach and named no attacker.
patterns.caveat: Same tools, different actors. ARTEX is open source, so a shared tool is a shared attribute, not a link between intrusions, and says nothing about who is behind them. The FBI and Talos both cite more than 2,250 downstream tenants but describe the case differently; that they are one case is our inference. The Commission did not name the tool, so it may not be any of those listed here.

edges.rel: same open-source tool (ARTEX), actor not shown same
same open-source tool (ARTEX), actor not shown same
AI tool used, tool not named

patterns.title: Developer and AI-agent toolchains as the target
patterns.narrative: Separate incidents aim at the tools developers and AI agents run with. Bitdefender found 22 GitHub links whose AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md files tell coding assistants to run a loader, and Google describes a North Korean cluster planting a backdoor through Claude Code settings files: the agent's own instruction files are now an attack route. A credential stealer sat in Microsoft's Agent Framework package on PyPI, and trojanized Claude Code extension builds reached Cursor's marketplace cache. A study of 428 LLM API routers found some injecting code and misusing credentials, and researchers took over the Kokoro model's Hugging Face account through an expired domain. Microsoft showed in a lab how a phished device-code approval could steer a coding agent. The prize in each is the keys and tokens these tools hold.
patterns.caveat: These are different actors and methods; no source connects them. The Microsoft device-code work, the router study and the Kokoro takeover are research, not attacks seen in the wild; the Kokoro researchers did not upload altered weights.

patterns.title: Reused passwords and phished device codes open accounts
patterns.narrative: Several services saw accounts opened with credentials rather than exploits. Hydro-Québec says an intruder used email and password pairs from elsewhere and asked about 1.7 million customers to reset passwords; Japan's Takarakuji lottery had 4,436 accounts entered in a password list attack; Germany's BundID citizen accounts faced a mass automated login wave and were blocked as a precaution; TfL took its Oyster photocard site offline after account compromises. Separately, Hornetsecurity describes device-code phishing in which victims enter a code on Microsoft's real sign-in page and hand tokens to the attacker, the same technique Microsoft showed against coding agents. Marathon Health, which runs Boone County's employee clinic, says a voice-phishing call gave an attacker access to its systems. Multifactor sign-in and blocking device-code flow where it is not needed answer both.
patterns.caveat: Different attackers and services; no source connects them. TfL has not said how accounts were compromised, and BundID officials see no evidence that data was taken. The Microsoft coding-agent case is a lab demonstration.

patterns.title: Outage wave: close in time, causes self-reported, and real knock-on harm
patterns.narrative: Outages hit well-known US services within a week: Microsoft 365, the FAA ground stop, the National Weather Service, Workday, Chase, United, Marriott, Charles Schwab, Apple and the NSA's classified network, with Japan's Docomo failing on Nov 16. NBC reported on Nov 19 that an NSA outage was still under way and, citing sources, not cyber-caused. The outages are linked only by timing. Where a cause was given it was the organisation's own, most often a planned change: a capacity upgrade at Microsoft, a router fault at the FAA, a software release at Chase, maintenance and, per the DNI, a PHP patch at the NSA. Officials see no cyberattack: DNI Jay Clayton told a House hearing there is "no evidence that this is a coordinated cyberattack or state-sponsored activity" and blamed maintenance and technical changes. The Microsoft outage did cause stated harm: attackers used it as a phishing lure, and a hotel report says it blocked a chlorine alert email before 15 guests were poisoned. Lawmakers are pressing for explanations.
patterns.caveat: Officials say these were not attacks and not coordinated. Workday, Marriott, Schwab and United published no cause, Google disputes a broad Gmail outage, and the FAA trigger is undetermined. That NBC's Nov 19 report describes the same NSA outage as the Nov 17 NSA Net failure is our inference. The hotel report comes from one outlet. The Microsoft outage itself began on Nov 12, just before this window.

edges.rel: a day apart, no stated link
likely the same NSA outage, not stated

patterns.title: Refrigeration controllers in the crosshairs, and Iran accused in several regions
patterns.narrative: Midnight Blue says attack waves on internet-exposed refrigeration controllers started in France on Oct 11, and this week disclosed six unpatched pre-authentication flaws in Danfoss controllers. In the UK, Pen Test Partners says a serious flaw in RDM refrigeration controllers led NCSC to issue an urgent alert to supermarkets, and that a quiet operation to patch exposed systems has largely mitigated it, though smaller cold-chain operators may still be exposed. VulnCheck disclosed 14 flaws in end-of-life Copeland XWEB EVO supervisors and saw two targeted within a day. France says it will seek EU sanctions on an IRGC cyber unit over the French attacks, and Italy's prime minister briefed the opposition on hybrid threats after supermarket and school incidents. In Washington, DHS testimony says Iran-linked actors have stepped up activity against US transport, healthcare, water, energy and financial networks since the US-Iran war began. The UAE's cybersecurity chief said Iran used data-wiping malware in attempts against UAE electricity, water, desalination, education and healthcare systems.
patterns.caveat: The attribution to an IRGC unit is the French government's; Iran routinely denies such operations and Midnight Blue says attribution remains open. No source ties the Copeland probing or the US activity to the French campaign; linking the French and US accusations is our inference from the shared accused state. The October attacks themselves are outside the map's window. No source ties the UK RDM work to the French attacks or to Iran; it is grouped by device class. The UAE statement was made at a conference and comes with no technical detail.

edges.rel: controllers hit in French attack waves

patterns.title: Government networks: long-hidden intrusions and state-linked espionage
patterns.narrative: Several governments disclosed intrusions this week. Bulgaria says unidentified hackers sat in state networks from 2021 and took over 62 million pages of documents. Nextgov reports USDA took applications offline for days and reset database passwords in every environment after an internal security incident. South Korea's Interior Ministry says the government's administrative email system was hacked through weak local-government networks and a single sign-on flaw, with abnormal access to about 300 accounts. Lithuanian customs suspended an authentication portal after unauthorised access. CloudSEK says the Silent Lynx group took over two thousand Tajik Defence Ministry documents through a railway employee's account. The European Commission confirmed an AI-assisted attack that took down HR and health-insurance systems. On the research side, Google says the PRC-nexus ARMORY CASTLE exploited a vCenter zero-day for espionage; Rapid7 attributes a stealthy SoftEther VPN bridge to Webworm, which targets European governments; Bitdefender's EggStreme backdoor still targets Philippine government bodies; Unit 42 and Kaspersky describe espionage over HTTP/3 and through GitHub and SharePoint; Google shows Russia's COLD RELIC using data stolen from one US organisation to phish another. On North Korea, Genians ties a NodeLinkRAT campaign to Kimsuky, Google describes a cluster backdooring crypto developers, and Talos tracks a crypto-stealing group it ties to North Korea with low confidence.
patterns.caveat: Bulgaria, USDA, South Korea, Lithuania and the Commission have named no attacker, and nothing ties them to each other or to the research reports; USDA's incident rests on anonymous sources and an internal email. Attributions are the vendors' own, at moderate or low confidence for Webworm, Kimsuky and Talos's cluster. The research reports are grouped by type and some describe older activity. CloudSEK links Silent Lynx to Kazakhstan with moderate confidence, and that report reached us via BES.media relaying Reuters.

patterns.title: Sector clusters: hospitals and late breach notices, and a run of South Korean university breaches
patterns.narrative: Healthcare filed the most breach notices on file this week, and two attacks disrupted care directly. The Greiz-Ronneburg district hospital in Germany closed its emergency room on Nov 15 after an extortion attack, and Monadnock Community Hospital in New Hampshire diverted ambulances after a phone and network outage it now confirms was a cyber incident. Most other notices describe intrusions found months earlier: Access Dental Management (341,049 people, May), Valley Family Health Care and LifeTouch Health (March), MPOWERHealth (June 2025), Hood River Dental (two incidents, 2025 and January 2026), Lansing Urgent Care (September), Dorsata (August, through a Metabase zero-day) and Geisinger (August). Atticus Administration's claims database for New York City retirees and Marathon Health's clinic systems were reached through providers. Social Security numbers and treatment details recur, so these feed fraud and extortion long after the intrusion. Chile's Hospital Clínico de la Universidad de Chile also reported affected systems and booking channels down. Separately, South Korean education disclosed one breach after another: Inje University (24,011 records from a class-site server), Paichai University (LMS and academic system), Jeonju University's AHA service (about 180,000 records), POSTECH (19,978 records through two portals, found via an illegal mining program) and the Jeonbuk education office's school bus system with student addresses. Victoria's privacy regulator found that one compromised school's system reached a database covering every government school student. Student portals and learning systems hold contact data that feeds voice phishing, which several of the universities warn about.
patterns.caveat: These are separate organisations and attackers; the sector is the only shared attribute and grouping them is our inference. Notice dates reflect US reporting rules, so the count says more about disclosure timing than about attack volume. INC Ransom's claim on Lansing Urgent Care is the group's, not the clinic's. No source links the Korean university breaches to one attacker, flaw or supplier; they are grouped by sector and because they were disclosed within a week, and most rest on DailySecu or Kyunghyang reporting of the institutions' notices. Counts are records, not people.

direct: NGINX Open Source and Plus from 1.9.5 with HTTP/2 can be made to run code as the nginx worker without a login; fixes are in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9, and proof-of-concept code is public for one flaw.
downstream: Xint chained one flaw with an unpatched Linux kernel SCTP bug to reach root and escape a Docker container, so a web front end can become a host compromise.

NGINX is embedded in load balancers, Kubernetes ingress controllers and appliances that update on their vendors' schedules; Synology has already listed the same CVE in DSM, so expect more appliance advisories.
watch_for: Ingress and appliance vendors shipping fixed NGINX builds
Worker crashes on HTTP/2 traffic
A Linux kernel fix and CVE for the SCTP flaw
Reports of in-the-wild exploitation
Appliance advisories naming CVE-2026-123007

direct: An unauthenticated attacker can bypass authentication on VMware vCenter Server (CVE-2026-123890, CVSS 9.8); Google says ARMORY CASTLE exploited it as a zero-day, and Rapid7 reports activity from as early as September. Fixes include vCenter 8.0 U3m; there is no workaround.
downstream: vCenter controls every virtual machine it manages, so one compromised server can expose a whole virtual estate.
Exploitation predates the fix, so patching does not show whether a server was already entered; logs back to September matter.
watch_for: vCenter servers reachable from untrusted networks
Unexpected vCenter sign-ins or new local accounts
Hunting guidance and indicators from Google and Broadcom
Victims named in follow-up reporting

direct: PLAID suspended all KARTE services after unauthorized access on Nov 13; account emails and integration credentials are listed as leaked, along with part of the data customers imported.
downstream: DHC says about 19.11 million customer records and BASE FOOD about 710,000 customers' names and emails leaked through KARTE.
Integration credentials held by the service may open customers' own systems, and leaked customer lists feed targeted phishing in Japanese.
watch_for: Further KARTE customers announcing leaks
Phishing that uses shop names and dates of birth
Use of integration keys connected to KARTE

direct: Account and billing data for every Fireworks AI account created before Oct 30 was exposed; some customers' secrets, model files and datasets were reached earlier.
downstream: Cursor, Notion and Uber are reported as affected customers; keys held by the provider led to a trojanized extension at Cursor.
Credentials pasted into AI prompts or held by inference providers can open systems far from the provider itself.
watch_for: Notices from AI and inference providers you use
Use of API keys issued to providers
Secrets in AI chat logs and traces

direct: Any service that decodes untrusted Base64 on an affected x86-64 HotSpot Java runtime could be crashed or taken over without a login.
downstream: Java is bundled inside third-party applications, appliances and container images, so exposure extends to products you did not build.
Patching depends on each vendor shipping an updated runtime, so some systems will stay exposed after your own servers are fixed.
watch_for: Unexpected JVM crashes and restarts
Vendor advisories naming a bundled Java runtime
Signs of exploitation reported by CISA or vendors

direct: Self-hosted Confluence Data Center with the Remote API enabled can be taken over without a login; CISA lists the Axis flaw as exploited.
downstream: In the case Rapid7 saw, the intruder took database credentials, queried a cloud data warehouse and signed in to Microsoft 365 as a service account.
Apache Axis 1.x is end-of-life and may sit inside other Java products that will not get a fix.
watch_for: Unusual Remote API requests to Confluence
Service accounts signing in from new places
Other products bundling Apache Axis 1.x

direct: Internet-facing N-central servers were exploited through zero-days published without coordinated disclosure; crypto miners were deployed.
downstream: An RMM server reaches every managed client, so a compromise can spread to many customer networks at once.
Removal of the Legacy API may break older integrations that still depend on it.
watch_for: N-central servers not on Hotfix 3
New agents or scripts pushed from RMM
Mining processes on managed endpoints

direct: Malicious JavaScript was injected into some Optimizely Web Experimentation customer projects, reaching 178 organisations by one researcher's count.
downstream: Coverage says the code skimmed payment cards and swapped crypto addresses on customers' sites, so their visitors were the victims.
Sites that load third-party scripts without integrity checks or a strict Content-Security-Policy inherit the supplier's compromise.
watch_for: Unexpected scripts on checkout pages
CSP violation reports
Notices from script and tag vendors

direct: Six unpatched pre-authentication flaws let attackers take over Danfoss AK-SM800A refrigeration controllers; hundreds are reachable online.
downstream: Food retail, cold storage and pharmacies risk spoiled stock and safety incidents; French attacks on such controllers were linked to fires.
France is seeking EU sanctions over the campaign, which could prompt further attacks or warnings.
watch_for: Refrigeration controllers reachable from the internet
Unexpected setpoint or alarm changes
CVE numbers and fixes from Danfoss
Advisories for other refrigeration controller brands, as with RDM in the UK

direct: Equinor's IT systems are under an ongoing attack; it says production is unaffected and email was reported down.
downstream: Restoration time is unknown, so partners and suppliers may see delays or unusual messages from Equinor.
Attackers often use a known incident to send fake invoices or updates in the victim's name.
watch_for: Messages claiming to come from Equinor
Norwegian authority advisories
Any named attacker or leak claim

brief/latest.headline: Exploited vCenter and Cisco Expressway flaws are due for patching by 23 November
brief/latest.plain_summary: Two flaws in widely used server software are being attacked and are on CISA's must-patch list with a 23 November deadline: VMware vCenter and Cisco Expressway. Google attributes the vCenter attacks to a suspected state-linked group. Separately, a supplier breach at PLAID has exposed customer data at many Japanese firms. Organisations running the affected products should patch now; others need no action beyond watching for phishing.

items.title: Google: vCenter zero-day CVE-2026-123890 used in espionage
items.why: Google says a suspected PRC-nexus group exploited this unauthenticated bypass from early September, and CISA lists it with a 23 November deadline.
items.action: Apply Broadcom's fixed vCenter builds (8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0200 or 9.1.1.0200) now; vCenter 7.0 has no public patch. Restrict inbound access to and egress from vCenter, following the hardening advice in Google's post.

items.title: Cisco Expressway CVE-2026-76466 exploited after public PoC
items.why: F6 reports an attack on clustered devices after a PoC was posted; Cisco's advisory still says it knows of no malicious use, and CISA's deadline is 23 November.
items.action: If you run clustered Expressway, upgrade to X15.5.20 now (X14 and earlier must move to a fixed release; Cisco says no workaround). If you cannot patch at once, F6 advises blocking TCP 4371-4372 except from trusted cluster node IPs.

items.title: NGINX HTTP/2 flaws allow remote code execution; PoC public
items.why: CERT-FR says two flaws allow unauthenticated code execution over HTTP/2 and a public proof of concept exists for one.
items.action: Check every NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus server that serves HTTP/2. Apply the fixed versions from F5 bulletins K000163926 and K000163928 (1.30.7 or 1.31.9), or disable HTTP/2 until patched. Review exposed servers for signs of compromise.

items.title: WordPress 7.1.5 fixes unauthenticated privilege escalation
items.why: The security release lists 20 items, including a flaw the project says could lead to remote code execution; no exploitation is reported.
items.action: Update WordPress to 7.1.5 now (Dashboard, Updates), or confirm the background auto-update ran; older branches are being backported, so watch for those releases.

items.title: ZOZO: about 15.18 million customers affected by PLAID KARTE leak
items.why: A breach at supplier PLAID's KARTE service has exposed customer data at ZOZO and other Japanese firms; card data is not confirmed leaked.
items.action: ZOZO customers: be wary of phishing emails, texts or calls impersonating ZOZO, and do not open their links or attachments, as ZOZO advises.

items.title: European Commission confirms AI-generated cyber campaign
items.why: The Commission says several applications were taken down, most are restored, and it has found no evidence of a staff-wide data breach.
items.action: If you work with EU institutions, expect notices from them and treat unexpected messages claiming to be from Commission staff with care.

items.title: Proximus mobile disruption: software bug, cyberattack ruled out
items.why: Proximus says a software update caused the disruption and rules out a cyberattack, per Belgian press reports.
